thread:
incident-bot: PagerDuty alert fired: `PD#67890` — severity: P1. Alert reason: repeated CUDA driver timeouts resulting in GPU hang + KV-cache invalidation on pool gpu-prod-92. Trigger: 5xx spikes & >80% GPU error rate across region-us-west-2.

pagerduty: Incident created: PD#67890 -> routed to eng-oncall. Escalation policy: gpu-hardware -> oncall (maria-j) -> if unacked 5m escalate to aj.

maria-j: Acked PD#67890. I'm on it. quick read: metric graphs show spike at 20:12 UTC, sustained for ~3m. Rolling errors labeled `CUDA_TIMEOUT` and `nvlink_err`.

sarah-k: Seeing increased 503s from hosted API routes /v1/generate for several customers. Logs show model-flight fallback to cpu-fallback-1 leading to 5–10x latency.

devon: +1. Dedicated pools also reporting request aborts; kvcache miss rate spiked after driver resets. Could be GPU hang -> kernel timed out -> driver reset -> processes killed.

maria-j: TL;DR: driver timeout on node gpu-92-3. Plan: (1) isolate node, (2) reroute traffic off pool gpu-prod-92, (3) attempt controlled driver restart and kvm cache warmup, (4) if unstable, evict instance and reprovision.

ops-bot: Automated action: mark pool gpu-prod-92 as `draining` (no new allocations). Command: `rdctl pool update gpu-prod-92 --state draining` executed.

maria-j: Running quick checks. `ssh jump@gpu-92-3` -> `sudo dmesg | tail -n 40` shows repeated `NVRM: Xid (PCI:0000:00:01): 31, Ch 00000001, Engine 0000000e` and `GPU watchdog timeout` lines.

aj: Oncall standby. If restart doesn't help escalate to hw-team. Noted.

sarah-k: Customer impact note: AcmePay (hosted, route id r-77) reporting 503s from 20:12–20:22 UTC; we've throttled retries but some requests backed up. I pushed a temporary customer status note to dashboard: "Degraded: inference latency increased for subset of requests in US-WEST-2".

devon: Suggest hotfix: update routing policy to prefer gpu-prod-44 / gpu-prod-12 for r-77 and other high-SLA routes. Command I will run: `rdctl route reroute --route r-77 --prefer gpu-prod-44,gpu-prod-12 --force`

maria-j: Do it. Also please sanity-check memory on those targets before moving high QPS.

devon: Pre-check: `rdctl pool metrics gpu-prod-44 | jq .gpu_free_mem` -> looks healthy (70% free). Proceeding.

ops-bot: Action log: `rdctl route reroute --route r-77 --prefer gpu-prod-44,gpu-prod-12 --force` executed by devon at 20:18 UTC.

pagerduty: PD#67890 note: ack by maria-j at 20:16 UTC.

sarah-k: Customer comms: CS drafted an update for AcmePay. Pinged @cs for review.

csm-bot: CS notified. Draft link: https://redwood.app/cs-drafts/PD-67890-acmepay-downtime

maria-j: Attempting controlled reset: `sudo nvidia-smi -pm 1 && sudo systemctl restart nvidia-persistenced && sudo modprobe -r nvidia_uvm && sudo modprobe nvidia_uvm` — running now. Watchdog suggests the process might orphan kvcache; we'll watch for KV cache population metrics.

20:20 UTC — maria-j: Driver restart returned clean. `nvidia-smi` shows GPU back online but we've lost approx 90% of kvcache entries for that pool. Expect cache-warmup latency.

devon: Observed temporary surge in latency as traffic rerouted and kvcache misses. Error rate on pool gpu-prod-92 dropped but r-77 still sees elevated latencies on a small fraction of traces.

aj: Good containment so far. Any signs of hardware fault (ECC errors, persistent Xid 31)?

maria-j: No ECC spikes. Xid 31 commonly a watchdog; could be model step causing long kernel. Will capture a core next time. For now stable.

ops-bot: Automated remediation suggestion: apply `auto-shed` for low priority routes hitting gpu-prod-92 to reduce new allocations while cache warms. Suggestion accepted by maria-j.

maria-j: I've applied shed rule: `rdctl pool update gpu-prod-92 --max-allocs 2 --shed-low-priority`

sarah-k: Monitoring customer-facing SLOs. Post-reroute: 503s normalized for AcmePay, but we see sustained 2–3s tail latency for chat endpoints for small subset. Adding to post-incident notes.

devon: FYI running healthcheck loop on node: `sudo /opt/redwood/bin/gpu-healthcheck --capture --samples 5` -> all checks passing. No kernel oops.

maria-j: Moving to 1:1 handoff: I'm going to bubble to hw-team for a deeper diagnostic tomorrow. For now I'll transition oncall to aj after containment.

aj: Taking over incident. I'll watch for reoccurrence and coordinate with hw-team. maria-j -- thanks for quick isolation.

20:32 UTC — aj: PD#67890 placed note: `contained - driver restart resolved immediate hang; cache loss caused elevated latency; traffic rerouted.` Next steps: schedule follow-up with hw-team and backend to add graceful kvcache prewarm on pool rejoin.

sarah-k: Filing a customer postmortem snippet and RCA starter. Noting: root-cause probable heavy NV kernel execution triggering GPU watchdog; mitigation: route controls + driver restart + kvcache prewarm.

devon: Suggest adding an SLO-exempt fallback less costly than CPU fallback to avoid 10x latency. Putting proposal in infra backlog.

ops-bot: Automated metrics note: 5xx spike window 20:12–20:20 UTC, peak error rate 12%.

aj: Closing PD for now (note: monitor 2h). If we see another Xid 31 within that window escalate to hw oncall.

maria-j: Leaving handoff comments: commands run, logs saved to `/var/log/redwood/incidents/PD-67890/` and a tarball uploaded to internal incident drive.

sarah-k: Thanks everyone. I'll sync with CS to finalize customer messages and send an update in 30m. :thumbsup:

devon: One last check: `rdctl pool set-annotation gpu-prod-92 health=quarantined` so automation won't auto-scale it back into rotation during post-incident churn.

ops-bot: Action recorded.

aj: I'm going to put a short incident note in #postmortems and tag hw + runtime teams. We'll reconvene if PD re-fires.

incident-bot: PD#67890 closed by aj (containment) at 20:40 UTC.

maria-j: Outbound: thanks team, especially devon for rapid reroute. Logging handoff in the incident tracker.

-- end of thread --
